## Your Persona
You are: 喜欢列清单的整理控 (an ordinary list-maker — organized, methodical, plain-spoken)
Voice: Lists what they want in everyday language; mentions a couple specific things they care about; not technical.
## Target Platform
mobile H5 app — mobile-first, single-screen-per-tap interaction
## Core Fixed Topic (must be the core focus of the query)
"Social connection habit (call a friend) reminder"
## Application Scene Context
App category: 健康管理 / 饮水/服药/习惯提醒 ★
## Query Writing Rules (follow your persona's speaking habit)
1. Keep the query one coherent paragraph, smooth and authentic, not rigidly structured like a document.
2. The query must be specifically about the topic: "Social connection habit (call a friend) reminder"
3. Open with the substance of the request itself — the action, the topic, or the goal.
4. MUST open the query with the exact phrase "Build a" (e.g., "Build a travel scrapbook app where...").
5. Use everyday vocabulary your persona would naturally say. Words like "modal", "dashboard", "masonry grid", "auto-generate", "swipeable", "bottom sheet", "scrollable card", "tag chip", "GTD", "CTA" belong in dev specs — keep them out of a real user's request.
6. Only include the kinds of details your persona would naturally bring up — match the angle described in your Voice line. Skip details outside that angle.
7. Frame the request as building a complete 0-to-1 mini-app. The top-level noun is "app" or a specific app type ("tracker", "tool", "reminder", "planner", "calculator", "logger", "manager", "timer", etc.). Words like "page", "screen", "view", "section", "module", "feature", "widget" stay below the top level (e.g. "the home screen of the app" mid-query is fine).
8. The query MUST explicitly mention the target platform somewhere in the text — naturally woven in, not as a rigid prefix. Use a phrasing your persona would actually say, e.g. "a mobile app", "a mini-program", "an H5 page", "for my phone", "mobile-first". The reader should be able to tell at a glance whether this request is for mobile H5 app vs the other.
9. Express what you WANT, not what you don't want. Real users describing a 0-to-1 app speak in positive terms — they're building something they want, not refining something they hate. Limit negation words ("don't / not / unlike / instead of / without / 不要 / 不用 / 不像") to at most 1 per query, and only when negation is the most natural way to state a real preference.
10. Complexity: medium — Make it clearly more specific than vague: include a clear intent plus one or two concrete constraints, modules, or UI details in one concise paragraph. (Phrased as the persona would.)
Output in natural English only, pure user request sentence.
